headline: Trump confirms on Fox News that the US hit an Iranian anti-aircraft facility on Qeshm Island last night
dek: Trump said US forces watched Iran build an anti-aircraft facility for about two months and 'as soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely'; he called it 'just a minor attack. It wasn't war', said 'I'm not looking to kill lots of people, but if we have to, we'll have to', claimed…
sources: US President Donald Trump, telephone interview on Fox News' Fox & Friends, relayed by Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Was last night a 'minor' defensive hit that keeps the deal alive, or proof the US is striking while talking -- and does anyone actually control Hormuz?

sections.what_happened: Trump said US forces watched Iran build an anti-aircraft facility for about two months and 'as soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely'; he called it 'just a minor attack. It wasn't war', said 'I'm not looking to kill lots of people, but if we have to, we'll have to', claimed Iran has 'no airplanes' and 'no anti-aircraft' left, and (per The Times relay) claimed the US has 'total control' of the Strait of Hormuz. This is the first on-camera presidential confirmation of the Qeshm strike previously reported by WSJ/AP/CNN from unnamed US officials as a limited defensive strike after Iranian surface-to-air fire at US assets. No damage assessment, casualty figure, or facility imagery has been published in the reports checked. PortWatch note: the newest IMF PortWatch snapshot (2026-10-26) is STALE -- it counted 4 transits through Hormuz on 2026-10-18, 7-day average 3.7 vs a 2025 baseline of 85.5/day -- so no current counted transit figure exists to test Trump's 'total control' claim; do not present any claimant transit number as counted.
sections.what_verified: 4 declared families carry the verbatim quotes: Al Jazeera, Gulf News, Dawn, and AFP (via Gulf Today)
sections.what_disputed: Tehran's position the same hour: SNSC Secretary Rezaei's X post (1900-02) says the US response to Iran's seven conditions 'was not convincing' and Hormuz reopens only when they are fully addressed and acted on. IRGC claims (1800-02, HELD) of 3 tankers mined and drones downed remain unverified and contradict a 'total control' picture. IMO Secretary-General Dominguez (recorded 1200-02) said the IMO cannot confirm minefields cleared and advised ships not to transit.
sections.why_matters: Trump, on Election Day, finally owns the Qeshm strike on camera -- then shrinks it: 'minor attack, wasn't war.' He says the US watched the air-defence site go up for two months and flattened it the night it finished. Tehran answers the same hour: no deal until all seven conditions are met. A strike and a deal, in the same breath -- which one is real?
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog 14:31 GMT = 18:31 ; Gulf Today published 18:30 , AFP-carried; Dawn live relay; Gulf News liveblog) -- Trump confirms on Fox News that the US hit an Iranian anti-aircraft facility on Qeshm Island last night: 'just a minor attack. It wasn't war'

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump, on Election Day, finally owns the Qeshm strike on camera -- then shrinks it: 'minor attack, wasn't war.' He says the US watched the air-defence site go up for two months and flattened it the night it finished. Tehran answers the same hour: no deal until all seven conditions are met. A strike and a deal, in the same breath -- which one is real? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Was last night a 'minor' defensive hit that keeps the deal alive, or proof the US is striking while talking -- and does anyone actually control Hormuz?
